draft.title: The Five Pillars
card: The Five Pillars are five core acts of worship and commitment that Muslims practise. They give Muslim life a shared structure.
The shahada is the declaration of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is his messenger. Salat is prayer, performed five times a day.
Zakat is giving a set share of wealth to those in need. Sawm is fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan.
Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca. Muslims who are able to go, in health and with enough money, are expected to make it at least once.
draft.remember: Five acts: declare faith, pray, give, fast, and make pilgrimage.

a.q: Which Pillar is the practice of giving a set share of wealth to people in need?
a.why: Zakat is the Pillar of giving to those in need. Sawm is tempting because it is also linked to self-discipline, but it means fasting during Ramadan, not giving wealth.
a.clue: Think of the Pillar that deals with money.

b.q: Samira, a Muslim in Perth, stops eating and drinking from dawn to sunset throughout Ramadan. Which Pillar is she practising?
b.why: Fasting from dawn to sunset in Ramadan is sawm. Salat is the tempting wrong answer because many Muslims pray more during Ramadan, but prayer is not the act of fasting that Samira is carrying out.
b.clue: Which Pillar involves going without food and drink?
